statement: Let words(s) be the list of maximal contiguous non-space blocks of the byte slice s. For a byte sequence w, let count_s(w) be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(words(s)) and words(s)[j] = w. Say w is uncommon for (s1,s2) if (count_s1(w) = 1 and count_s2(w) = 0) or (count_s1(w) = 0 and count_s2(w) = 1). Whenever uncommon_from_sentences(s1,s2) returns a result r, for every byte sequence w, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(r) and r[i] = w is 1 if w is uncommon, and 0 otherwise. Thus r lists every uncommon word exactly once, in arbitrary order, and no other byte sequence.
preconditions: s1 and s2 are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) satisfying the problem constraints: 1 <= len(s1), len(s2) <= 200; every byte of s1 and s2 is an ASCII lowercase letter (byte value 97 through 122) or a space (byte value 32); s1 and s2 have no leading or trailing space; and consecutive words are separated by exactly one space.

statement: For every s1 and s2 satisfying the preconditions, uncommon_from_sentences(s1,s2) returns a result r; the call does not fail (no arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic).
preconditions: s1 and s2 are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) satisfying the problem constraints: 1 <= len(s1), len(s2) <= 200; every byte of s1 and s2 is an ASCII lowercase letter (byte value 97 through 122) or a space (byte value 32); s1 and s2 have no leading or trailing space; and consecutive words are separated by exactly one space.
